A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same canopy-height estimation study. The complete 17-page documents, including figures, tables, mathematical notation, and Appendices A-D, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model evaluations in Section 4, ablation experiments in Appendix B, and deforestation-area analysis in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 reports the same original model evaluations, appendix ablations, and deforestation-area analysis. Retaining these results does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same 3D U-Net, monthly Sentinel-2 inputs, repeated Sentinel-1 composite, modified Huber loss with track shifting, and smoothing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same European 2019-2022 Sentinel/GEDI coverage, ALS examples, and Copernicus forest-type data. No datasets, tasks, populations, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding external comparisons retain Liu, Tolan, Lang, Pauls, and Turubanova, including the appendix forest-type comparison. The same 2D/3D stack/composite baseline configurations are evaluated.

E3.justification: Training and evaluation settings match, including 400,000 training iterations, batch size 16, the subset/full-dataset distinction, 1,500 validation locations, map resampling, and height thresholds. Appendix experimental protocols also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical spectral-band ablations, monthly activation visualizations, forest-type comparisons, and seasonal-input experiments in Appendix B. Height-dependent error analyses and deforestation case studies and analyses are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains the same year-to-year standard-deviation reporting, and Tables 6 and 8 retain the same plus/minus reporting practice. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 4 retains the proposed model's MAE of 4.76 m, MSE of 74.28 m², and R² of 0.591; appendix ablation scores and deforestation-area estimates are also identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical descriptions and definitions are unchanged. Neither version contains a theorem-and-proof development, and v3 adds no formal assumptions, derivations, or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about 10 m European temporal canopy-height maps, improved 2020 estimates and tall-tree accuracy, and benefits from monthly imagery over composites.

C2.justification: Interpretations of seasonal information, geolocation shifts, and tall-tree performance remain identical. Both retain the difficulty of detecting small growth over a short period and the qualification that monthly activation patterns require further investigation.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware disclosures, Appendix A's storage and CPU/GPU inference details, and code, weights, and map access information are unchanged. The added CTrees support acknowledgment supplies no new reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior canopy-height and temporal-imagery research are unchanged. CTrees is added as an acknowledged supporter, not as a research reference.

P1.justification: v3 adds one sentence acknowledging support from CTrees and its website. Apart from the updated arXiv version/date stamp, the remaining prose, terminology, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgments now continue onto page 9, shifting the Impact Statement downward. Figures 1-9 and Tables 1-8 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement; the layout change is limited.

improvement.justification: v3 adds support attribution and causes minor reflow on pages 8-9. The methods, empirical evidence, interpretations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, including the appendices. These limited administrative and presentation edits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
